## Goal
A person who wants only a phone number or an email address removed must get only what that needs: no per-site to-do for sites that cannot help, a letter that names only the value, and no name or address anywhere. The pieces are `tiers.value_applicable` and `lookup_pattern` (`engine/tiers.py:89-118`), `Runner.process` (`engine/runner.py:444-460`), `outbox.compose` for value-only profiles (`engine/outbox.py:162-168`) and `submitters/base.value_copy_fields`. Check `tests/test_bl_in_08_exposure.py` first; this WO tests the runner path with a fake registry, `FakeMailer` and a temporary store. Tests only; a defect is a finding with file:line and a strict xfail.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. With a registry of three brokers (one with a phone lookup pattern, one with only an email route, one with neither) and a phone-only person: the third produces no to-do and no `todo_created` event; the second queues a `value_removal` letter; the first is scanned only through the lookup (no name search).
2. The queued letter text contains the phone number the person allowed, the listing URLs and the removal mailbox, and contains no name, no street, no city, no age and no email address of the person (sentinels).
3. Without `allow_phone_disclosure` the letter is not composed and the run records a plain reason instead of leaking the number (`letters.value_letter_vars` raises `ValueError`, `letters.py:112-114`); assert what the runner does with that error and that no number appears in any Event.
4. An email-only person gets the same behaviour with the email address and without the phone.
5. After a send through `FakeMailer` with approval, the status moves to SUBMITTED and the Event details contain ids and enums only.
6. The `copy_fields` card for the person contains only value fields, listing links and the mailbox (`submitters/base.py:60-76`).
7. Sockets blocked; no browser (set the config so browser automation is off); `tmp_path` only.

**Limits (every Grok WO, CLAUDE-G-004):** offline only. No network, credentials, git or gh, installs, or running the real app against real sites or a real mailbox; never read anything outside the repo. Fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Tests pass on Windows too (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`). Check `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/`, `tests/grok/` and the in-house `tests/test_*.py` first; don't duplicate a guard.

Code rules (backend WOs; owner lane change 2026-11-09):

No contract changes: `models.py`, `interfaces.py`, `state.py`, `registry.py`, `storage/`, `schema/`, `cli.py`, `config.py`, `paths.py`, `netpolicy.py`, `consent.py`, `crypto.py`, `secrets.py`, `secret_backends.py`, `logging_setup.py`, `engine/browser.py`. - Front end and design stay in-house: never `src/freemyid/wizard/`, `src/freemyid/templates/`, `web/`, `brand/`.
- Offline: tests use fakes and `monkeypatch`. An autouse fixture in your test file makes `socket.socket.connect` and `socket.create_connection` raise. No subprocess, no real scheduler, browser or mailbox. Never run `freemyid run`, `send` or `schedule install`.
- Every existing test keeps passing unchanged. If your change correctly breaks an in-house or Codex test, stop and report it with file:line; never edit a test outside your allowed paths.
- Typed Python 3.11+, ruff-clean, small focused diff. Logs and events stay PII-free (counts and codes only). Fake people only. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing (2026-11-09); re-check them.
